 Oral Judgment

(Per: Hon'Ble Mr. Justice R.Nataraj) The claimants have filed this appeal challenging the
judgment and award dated 18.01.2021 passed in Mvc No.211/2016 by the Additional Senior Civil
Judge and Mact, Bidar [for short 'Tribunal'], seeking enhancement of compensation.
2.  The claimants are the legal heirs of deceased Omkar, who died in a road accident on 14.01.2016 when the offending vehicle dashed against him.

Hence, they filed claim petition before the Tribunal claiming compensation of Rs.81,50,000/- from the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle and contend that Omkar was aged 35 years and was a partner in Omkar and Sons and was earning Rs.1,60,000/- per annum from commission agency and Rs.2,50,000/- to Rs.3,00,000/- per annum from Agriculture.
3.
The insurer contested the claim petition and denied the accident as well as the involvement of the NC: 2026:KHC-K:1097-DB HC-KAR offending vehicle.
It also denied its liability to pay the compensation.
The claimant was examined as PW1 and Exs.P1 to P12 were marked.
A witness was examined as PW2.
Based on the oral and documentary evidence, the Tribunal held that the accident was due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the offending vehicle.

It also held that the deceased was aged 35 years at the time of accident and since there was no actual proof of the income earned by the deceased, it considered the notional income of the deceased at Rs.10,500/- per month and awarded the following compensation:
Loss of dependency Rs.20,16,000/-
 Loss of estate Rs.15,000/-
 Funeral expenses Rs.15,000/-
 Loss of consortium Rs.40,000/-
The Tribunal directed the insurer to pay the compensation along with interest at 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till the date of realisation.

Being NC:
2026:KHC-K:1097-DB HC-KAR aggrieved by the quantum of compensation awarded, the claimants are before the Court.
5. The learned counsel for the claimants contended that the deceased was a partner in Omkar Traders and was drawing annual remuneration of Rs.1,57,200/-.

He contends that Exs.P8 to P11 are the income tax extracts of Omkar and Sons, which shows that Nageshwari And Ors vs Sultan Iqbal Chaudary And Anr on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/120279142/
3 the deceased was paid a sum of Rs.1,57,200/- per annum as salary.

sentences.text: He therefore contends that the Tribunal ought to have considered the income of the deceased as Rs.1,57,200/- per annum and not as Rs.1,20,000/-.
He also contends that the Tribunal failed to award loss of parental consortium to the children of the deceased and filial consortium to the mother and father of the deceased.
He therefore contends that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal be enhanced.

6. Per contra, the learned counsel for the insurer submits that the claimants have marked Exs.P8 to P11, which are the returns filed by Omkar and Sons, which is a NC: 2026:KHC-K:1097-DB HC-KAR proprietary concern of Shamarao.
He contends that Shamarao is the father of the deceased Omkar and it highly improbable that the deceased was being paid an annual salary.

He also contends that Exs.P8 to P11 do not contain the salary paid to the deceased, but the same is shown in the statement of profit and loss, which is not an authenticated document and therefore cannot be relied upon.
He also contends that the claimants ought to have placed on record the returns filed by the deceased Omkar to establish that he was being paid a yearly salary of Rs.1,57,200/- per annum.
He thus contends that the Tribunal is justified in applying the notional income of Rs.10,500/- per month and determining the compensation.
Hence he submits that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and proper.
7. We have considered submissions of the learned counsel for the claimants and the learned counsel for the insurer.
NC: 2026:KHC-K:1097-DB HC-KAR 8.
A perusal of Exs.P8 to P11 shows the return filed by Omkar and Sons and the declarant claimed that he was the proprietor of Omkar and Sons.
Though it is mentioned in the statement of loss and profits that the deceased was being paid an yearly salary of Rs.1,57,200/- there is no other material to justify the same.
Furthermore, the ITR Forms filed do not correspond with the figures mentioned in the statement of profits and loss.
Therefore, the contention of the claimants that the deceased was earning Rs.1,57,200/- per annum cannot be believed.
Be that as it may, it is stated that the deceased was helping out his father in the grocery business.
Assuming that he was assisting his father in the business, it cannot be said that he was earning a notional income of Rs.10,500/- per month.
Therefore, this Court considers it appropriate to consider the notional income of the deceased at a sum of Rs.1,50,000/- per year.
The Tribunal considering the age of the deceased had rightly applied the multiplier of '16'.
As the deceased had left NC: 2026:KHC-K:1097-DB HC-KAR behind him his wife, there children and his mother, 1/4th of his income has to be deducted towards his personal and living expenses.
In addition, 40% of his income has to be added towards loss of future prospects.

Consequently, the compensation determined by the Tribunal deserves to be enhanced as under:
Rs.1,57,500/- x 16 = Rs.25,20,000/-

In view of the above, the following:
ORDER i) The appeal is allowed in part.

ii) The compensation of Rs.20,86,000/-
awarded by the Tribunal is enhanced to a sum of Rs.27,90,000/- which is payable by the insurer along with interest of the rate of 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till the date of realisation.
iii) The enhanced compensation shall be deposited by the insurer before the Tribunal within 30 days from the date of this judgment, failing which, the interest shall be charged 9% per annum from the date of claim petition till the date of realisation.
